rendered: The document does not say the EG process corrodes the aluminium foil. It reports the opposite: the EG-based process recovered the foil with no corrosion, indicating the process does not corrode aluminum.[1][2] The paper's general concern is that aluminium foils are reactive and easily corroded during separation, which contaminates the active materials.[3][4] The only corrosion the paper describes occurred in water, not in the EG process. Water was rejected because the foil corroded from lithium leaching out of the NMC cathode, which made the water solution basic.[5][6] The paper argues that corrosion of aluminium would contaminate the NMC particles through aluminium hydroxide precipitates that form on the cathode surfaces.[7][8] The paper does not describe any step that removes such a corrosion product. The only post-separation cleaning it describes is an alcohol rinse of the cathode to remove EG residues, and the recovered foils are reported as shiny with no residues left.[9][10][11]
